notes:
PERSEUS: Neither /hopper/about nor /hopper/opensource states a text license. The license is in the footer of each text page: 'This work is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0 United States License' linking to https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/us/ (verified on 14 of the 17 Perseus pages). Three pages carry NO CC footer: the Vulgate (1999.02.0060), Lewis & Short (1999.04.0059) and Allen & Greenough (1999.04.0001); these are listed with rights_status=unverified / link only. Stable URL pattern: https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus:text:<id>; ids are not all 1999.02.* (Loeb-derived texts are 2007.01.* / 2008.01.*). Perseus returns HTTP 200 even for wrong ids, so each page title was checked. Note Cicero In Catilinam lives inside the Clark Orationes volume 1999.02.0010 and needs ':text=Catil.:speech=1'. The 'edition description' printed in each page footer (editor, place, year) was used for editor/edition_year. Author_death_year uses negative integers for BC. The source XML of these texts is on GitHub (PerseusDL/canonical-latinLit) under CC BY-SA 4.0, which is a cleaner basis for hosting than the 3.0 US badge if the editor wants to redistribute. Scaife Viewer is behind an Anubis bot-challenge and could not be read.

CORPUS CORPORUM: The site is a single-page JavaScript app; curl of /home or /browser returns only a nav shell. The About/License text is embedded in https://mlat.uzh.ch/cc_modules/home.js and rendered at https://mlat.uzh.ch/home (section id='license'). There is no terms page (/about/ is an empty Apache index). Quoted license text: 'The data we transcribed ourselves (including some editions by Philipp Roelli) is published under Creative Commons Share-Alike and may thus be reused freely (but non-commercially) as long as the source is indicated. Most of the texts present here, however, stem from various online sources. As far as we could determine they are either in the public domain or their use was granted us by their owners. ... Texts may be downloaded as TEI xml for non-commercial use.' Patrologia Latina corpus (id 38) source is 'cf. Open Greek and Latin' http://opengreekandlatin.github.io/patrologia_latina-dev/. Because of the explicit non-commercial wording and unclear CC variant, all entries are rights_status=open_access_limited / hosting_allowed=false even though the Migne print text is public domain. Text URL pattern verified: https://mlat.uzh.ch/browser/<cc_id or idno> (302) -> https://mlat.uzh.ch/browser?path=<id> (200); the app's own permalink is host+'/browser/'+cc_id, e.g. https://mlat.uzh.ch/browser/cps_2.HieStr.ViSPaPr. Work/text ids were obtained from the JSON-less XML API https://mlat.uzh.ch/php_modules/navigate.php?load=/38/<author>/<work> and text rendering checked with php_modules/display_text.php?ajax=true&path=<id>. The Thomas Aquinas corpus (id 11975, mirrored from Corpus Thomisticum) is NOT accessible outside the UZH IP range. Bonaventura not found. The 'Regula cum commentariis' is Rule + commentary, not a clean Regula Benedicti.

CORPUS THOMISTICUM: no terms-of-use page; the only rights statement is the footer on each text page ('© 2019 Fundación Tomás de Aquino quoad hanc editionem. Iura omnia asservantur') and the homepage footer ('© 2000-2019 Fundación Tomás de Aquino. Iura omnia asservantur'). Index of works: https://www.corpusthomisticum.org/iopera.html. Summa Theologiae prima pars starts at sth1001.html; De ente et essentia at oee.html. Link only.
